tracks.narration: Walking a winding path across a hill — how fast does your altitude change?
Take f equals x squared plus y squared. The level curves are concentric circles. Walk the path gamma of t equals cos t plus one, sin t — a unit circle offset to the right.
As the particle moves, the gradient of f points outward from the origin, and the velocity gamma prime of t is tangent to the path. Their dot product is the rate of change of altitude.
Below the diagram, plot the altitude z of t against time. Its slope at every instant exactly matches the gradient dotted with velocity.
The multivariable chain rule is this: take the gradient at the point, dot it with the velocity along the path.
Gradient dot velocity. Slope along any path.
